title: Turn a wish into a goal
summary: A clear goal has an amount, a deadline and small steps you can follow.

variants.markdown:
**English draft for R5 review.**

Sana wants a new cycle that costs ₹3,000. Saying "I want a cycle" is a wish. A **goal** is clearer: "I will save ₹3,000 in 10 months."

A good goal has an amount, a deadline and steps. Sana divides ₹3,000 by 10 months. That is ₹300 a month, or about ₹75 a week. Now the big target feels like small **saving steps**.

Her grandfather gives ₹500 on her birthday. She adds it to her savings, and she can reach her goal a little sooner.

To **stay on track**, Sana marks her progress on a chart on the wall. After three months she has ₹900. Seeing the bar fill up keeps her going. If a month is tight and she saves less, she does not give up. She adjusts the deadline or saves a bit more later.

Goals work best when they are specific, small to start and checked often.

Gullak uses virtual play money only.

questions.prompt: Which one is a clear goal?

options.text: I will save ₹3,000 in 10 months for a cycle
I hope to get a lot of money

questions.explanation: A clear goal has an amount and a deadline. The second statement has both.

questions.prompt: Sana wants ₹3,000 in 10 months. How much should she save each month?
questions.explanation: ₹3,000 divided by 10 months is ₹300 a month.

questions.prompt: Sana saves less in one tight month. What is a good response?

options.text: Adjust the plan and keep going

questions.explanation: Goals can be adjusted. Checking progress and changing the plan helps you stay on track.
